You need three things to own a rifle:

A reason. (Hunting, target shooting, sport all allowable, self/home defence is NOT an allowable reason)

A place to shoot. (Own land, permission of land holder etc)

Membership of a recognised club.

Shooting rabbits, deer etc will be granted as a reason, but the rifle they let you buy must be suited to that game. i.e you wont get away with a .303 for hunting rabbits! You will only be allowed to own the type of rifle unless you present a new, provable reason for owning a different one. Also all ammunition you buy and own must be accounted for and there are strict limits to how much you can have.

In reality the best you will get away with in the UK, in ideal circumstances is a semi auto .223 of some description with a tiny magazine. You might be able to bluff something beefier for hunting deer, but you ll have to prove you actually, you know, hunt deer.

Shotguns are pretty easy to acquire for legal reasons (it is still an Englishman's right, enshrined in law, to own a shotgun. Firearm ownership is considered a 'privilege') I own a cheap, but well loved and cared for little O/U 12 gauge myself :)

EDIT: Just to clarify; before Dunblane you could get pretty much any reasonable firearm in the UK once you had successfully applied for a license: I had my eye on a S&W 629 just before it all went down.

Exceptions were called Section 5 firearms and covered things like full autos, large calibres and sawn off shotguns; and bizarrely stun guns and pepper sprays (Yes, technically you would get in just as much trouble for being caught with a Tazer as you would for an Uzi or a rocket launcher)
